tldr: In a balanced experiment with fixed categorical potential outcomes, equal roster margins and a public fixed occupancy bound \(M\), the original raw Gaussian \(L^1\) p-value has a uniform graph-residual calibration law. The exact-balance residual error is \(O_{M,\nu}(n^{-1/6})\) under the variance floor, and the realized estimated-covariance reference error is \(O_M(n^{-1/4})\). These laws determine nondegenerate critical rejection limits; slice concentration handles separated drift without a variance floor. A realizable cross-four and sharp-triple family gives a matched critical curve, and identical margins can give opposite accumulated calibration. A terminating rational Gaussian-score construction makes the compatible-table correction exactly finite weak-null valid. The algorithm and finite certificate terminate mathematically; practical implementation, useful runtime and power improvement are unclaimed.
